title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.4.0)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.4.0 (2026-10-23)

Search and the location map.

Added

  • "What fits?": a Fits section in Browse's More filters finds pieces by size, whatever their orientation: about this size (within a tolerance in mm or %, default 10 %, closest first) or can hold this size (every side at least the asked one, least waste first). Each row shows how far off it is or how much it wastes, as a share of the piece and in m3 (per piece on batches). The list can also sort by volume, and the card view has a sort menu.
  • Near: a Near section in Browse's More filters finds pieces around a point (a pasted "lat, lon"), by their current location or by their origin, within a radius in km or simply nearest first. Each row shows its distance, and the list sorts by it. A component page links to "Near this piece".
  • Origin coordinates: the origin form of a piece takes the latitude and longitude of its origin place; until now they could be set only when the piece was created. In every location form a pasted "lat, lon" fills both boxes, and a comma after the latitude moves on to the longitude.
  • Location Map: a new page next to the Similarity Map shows the pieces on a map, by their current location or by their origin, in clusters with counts. It takes the filters of Browse (with a "Show as list" link back), colours the pieces like the Similarity Map, opens a piece's preview on a click, and offers "Search near here" on a click into the map. The map images come from the tile server of FOSSGIS e.V. (tile.openstreetmap.de); only this page loads them.
  • Similar pieces: a card on the component page shows the six pieces nearest in shape, over the whole shape descriptor rather than on the two-dimensional Similarity Map; size counts as well as the outline. "Show more" brings up to 24. The nearest pieces are also available at GET /identities/{id}/similar, with every Browse filter applied before the ranking.
  • MCP: search_components takes fit_mode, size_mm and tolerance, near_lat, near_lon, near_layer and radius_km (each result with its distance), and sort and order; its description now says what the text query matches (name, id prefix, catalog number). The new tool catalog_overview counts the pieces of a search by material, original function, dataset, shape class and circulation, with the range of each side in mm, how many have a location and how many are not public. similar_components now ranks by the shape descriptor (with basis, count and the filters of search_components) instead of the distance on the Similarity Map.
  • Grasshopper: the new FetchSimilarComponents returns the pieces nearest in shape to a piece, with their distance, and takes the filters, the dimension search and the near search of FetchFilteredComponents. FetchFilteredComponents gains the dimension search (FitMode, FitSize, FitTolerance) and the near search (NearPoint, NearLayer, RadiusKm), with the deviation or waste (Fit) and the distance (DistanceKm) per result.
  • Grasshopper, texture colours: CreateComponentIdentity and CreateComponentSnapshot give a mesh the colours of its texture when it is staged: when the mesh comes from a Rhino object whose material has a base-colour image, each vertex takes the colour at its texture coordinate, on every level of detail. The texture replaces vertex colours the mesh already has, with a remark. Meshes without such a texture are staged as before. Grasshopper library 261022: run CSC_Update.

Changed

  • Registration: without open domains the catalog is invite only, and the register page then asks for an invitation code and suggests no open sign-up. With open domains the page says that registration is open to certain domains and lists them behind a "?"; no page names a fixed university any more. CSC_OPEN_REGISTRATION_DOMAINS is now empty by default: a server that keeps open registration must set it explicitly.
  • Privacy page and imprint: they state that the maintainer runs the catalog in person and is its sole controller, and that TU Darmstadt does not operate it and is not responsible for it. The privacy page names the tile server of the Location Map and what it receives, and no longer claims that nothing is loaded from other sites; the imprint cites the DDG instead of the repealed TMG. The Content-Security-Policy allows images from that one tile host in addition.
  • No Google map preview: pointing at a location in the Browse table no longer loads an embedded Google map; the location is a link that opens Google Maps in a new tab on a click. With no embed left, the Content-Security-Policy allows no frames (frame-src 'none').

Fixed

  • Browse table: at middle widths its columns no longer run into each other; the table keeps a minimum width for the columns shown and scrolls sideways inside its frame. The same for the admin Materials table.
  • Statistics: one piece with a malformed size in the database can no longer make the statistics (and with them Analytics) fail for everyone.

Security

  • Next.js 16.4.1: the web app moves from Next.js 16.4.0 to 16.4.1, which fixes two critical advisories (GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw, code execution through the image optimizer with SVG files; GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r, denial of service through Server Actions). The catalog was not reachable through either: it does not use the image optimizer and has no Server Actions. Upgraded as a precaution; npm audit is clean again.

Server notes

  • After the deploy, run scripts/db_maintenance/backfill_geo_points.py --apply once: it stores the location points the near search uses for the existing pieces (new and edited pieces get them on their own). Without --apply it only reports, and it exits with 4 while points are missing or out of date.
  • After the deploy, run the map job once (main_component_map.py, or --knn-only for the similarity data alone): until it has run, similar pieces answer 409 and the card stays hidden. The similarity data is then rebuilt with the map on every scheduled run; a new or reshaped piece joins at the next run.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
